title: Playwright Examples
description: Small Playwright examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: A browser test
examples.description: A browser test opens a page and checks what a person can do. setContent gives this test a tiny page without a website server.

examples.title: Find by role
examples.description: A role describes what an element does. A button role and its name make a locator that resembles how a person finds the control.

examples.title: Labels identify inputs
examples.description: A label tells a person what an input is for. getByLabel uses that relationship.

examples.title: Click an action
examples.description: click asks Playwright to perform a real user-like click. Check the visible result, not only that the click method returned.

examples.title: Assertions wait for a result
examples.description: Playwright locator assertions retry for a short time. This helps when a visible change happens after the action.

examples.title: Count repeated items
examples.description: A locator can match several elements. toHaveCount checks how many matches exist.

examples.title: Check a checkbox
examples.description: check sets a checkbox to checked. It is clearer than clicking when the desired state is known.

examples.title: Select an option
examples.description: A select input stores an option value. The label shown to people can differ from that value.

examples.title: Test keyboard access
examples.description: A keyboard test checks focus and key actions. It can reveal a control that works only with a mouse.

examples.title: Mock a page response
examples.description: A route handler can provide a known response. The test controls the content without calling a real external service.

examples.title: Isolate test state
examples.description: Each Playwright test normally gets a fresh browser context. A context separates saved state such as cookies between tests.

examples.title: Capture useful evidence
examples.description: A screenshot records visible state. It helps explain a failure but is not a replacement for a precise behaviour check.
